### Identification notes

Dicranum scottianum is a hyperoceanic moss, so it is confined to high rainfall districts and situations where there is constant high humidity and an equable temperature range. So, except for a few sites in the Weald, it is mainly confined to the western seaboard of Britain and Ireland.

The species it is most likely to be confused with, especially in the absence of mature capsules, is D. fuscescens. Habitat can provide some clues though, as D. fuscescens is far more tolerant of cold and exposed situations than D. scottianum.

One of the characters used by some well-known keys to identify D. scottianum – an entire or weakly denticulate upper leaf margin – does not work well with some plants which have toothed leaf margins, inviting confusion with D. fuscescens. Under the excellent key to European Dicranum published by Lars Hedenäs and Irene Bisang in 2004 (see Resources pages), two species, D. scottianum and D. canariense have a symmetrical (or nearly so) and straight capsule and incrassate upper cells. Plants with these characters but clearly dentate or denticulate upper leaf margins key out as D. canariense, a species now considered synonymous with D. scottianum.

Valonia utricularis (Roth) C. Agardh

Image

1, 3. In habitat, on fragment of dead branched corals. Hainan Island, Yalong Wan, March 2012. 2. Habit.

Thallus solitary, aggregate, prostrate, and partially erect, 1–3 cm high, translucent, bright green to deep dark green, comprised of branched filaments of macroscopic cells. Cells firm, not densely packed, small and large of various shape (saccate, spherical, cylindrical, oblong-clavate, or pyriform), arcuate, 3–7 mm in diameter, 5–20 mm long. Branching irregular, from all sides of parent cell. Attachment by minute branched rhizoids issuing from small basal cells. Growing on hard substrate in crevices, underneath of corals in the middle intertidal to upper subtidal zones (to 15 m depth) of semiprotected shores, or sometimes epiphytically on larger algae. Plants tightly adherent to paper when dried.

Distribution. Europe, North, Central, and South America, Atlantic islands, western Atlantic, Africa, Indian Ocean islands, South-west Asia, Asia (China, Taiwan, Japan), South-east Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Myanmar, Malaysia, Philippines, Indonesia), Australia and New Zealand, Pacific islands.

Valonia utricularis (Roth) C. Agardh 1823 (Figure 39).

Order: Cladophorales; Family: Valoniaceae.

Synonym: Valonia incrustans Kützing 1843.

Habitat: Found in the infralittoral zone (1–35 m depth), growing epilithically on coral substrates or within seagrass meadows.

Description: The thallus is an aggregate structure, both prostrate and partially erect, reaching 1–3 cm in height. It is translucent, displaying colors ranging from bright green to deep dark green, and consists of branched filaments made up of macroscopic cells.

These cells are firm but not densely packed, exhibiting a saccate form, which can vary between spherical, cylindrical, oblong-clavate, and pyriform shapes. They are arcuate, measuring 3–7 mm in diameter and 5–20 mm in length. Branching occurs irregularly from all sides of the parent cell. The plant attaches to surfaces via minute branched rhizoids that emerge from small basal cells. When dried, the plants adhere tightly to paper.

Situación taxonómica

Descripción

     Alga de color verde oscuro, con un talo formado por grandes células turgentes (utrículos) de forma esférica o tubular. El número de utrículos puede variar de unos pocos a muchos, dando lugar entonces a un césped compacto.

Hábitat

     Especie común, propia del mediolitoral y del infralitoral, apareciendo en fondos rocosos, umbríos y de fuerte hidrodinamismo. Suele formar parte del estrato basal que se encuentra por debajo de Cystoseira stricta, Laurencia papillosa o Corallina elongata.

Distribución

     Mediterráneo y Atlántico próximo.

Distribución regional

     Fácil de observar en los diferentes tramos costeros rocosos. Se la ha observado formando parte del estrato basal de la Comunidad fotófila de la roca infralitoral superior en régimen batido (RIFSB) (Mapas 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 y 7).
